  1
 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTIII)N  ADOPTING  THE  SCHEDULE  OF FEES  FOR  SERVICES

  PURPOSE:  The City  Council  will  conduct  a Public  Hearing  and consider  adopting  a Resolution
  approving  and  establishing  a new  schedule  of fees effective  for  FY  2025-26  and rescinding
  Resolution  No. 2021-51-CC.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council
  will  consider:
  1.  Adopting  the Resolution  establishing  a new  Schedule  of Fees for City  services  effective
  for FY 2025-26;
  2.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Resolution  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney;
  and
  3.  RescindingResolutionNo.2021-51-CC

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Staff  estimates  the  aggregate  adjustments  will  generate  approximately
  $500,000  in additional  annual General  Fund revenue,  improving  cost recovery  for services  affected
  by wage,  benefit,  and operating  cost increases  since 2021.  The estimate  reflects  the net effect  of
  the 7% baseline  adjustment  (where  legally  permissible),  offset  by exemptions  and rounding,  and
  does not presume  full utilization  of every  fee line. Actual  revenue  will  depend  on service  demand
  and compliance.

  BACKGROUND:  The City's  Master  Fee and Charges  Schedule  consolidates  fees for services
  authorized  by the Municipal  Code  and other  authorities.  The  last  comprehensive  update  was
  adopted  in FY 2021-22  (ResolutionNo.  2021-51-CC),  which  contemplated  periodic  inflationary
  adjustments  subject  to Council  approval.  Since that action,  fees have not been updated,  despite  the
  City's  costs  increasing  materially  (as  evidenced  by  cumulative  CPI  increases  since  2021).
  Departments  have  reviewed  their  fee inventories  and recommended  changes  to reflect  current
  service  delivery  methods,  staffing,  and program  structures.

  I

  9
 ANALYSIS:  Under  California  Constitution  Article  XIII  C, section  1(e)  (Proposition  26),  a fee
may recover  only the City's  reasonable  cost to provide  the service  and therefore  is not a tax. The
proposed  schedule  complies  with  this standard  by:

  Applying  a baseline  7% adjustment  to most fees to partially  restore  cost recovery  eroded
  since 2021.
  Exempting  fees that are voter-approved,  set by statute  or regulation,  or otherwise  legally
  constrained.
  *  Making  targeted  line-item  updates  to add new fees, retire obsolete  entries,  and correct  titles,
  units,  or administrative  notes.

Departments  reviewed  each  fee  and  its  cost  drivers  (labor,  time  standards,  materials,  and
overhead).  Where  a fee's  cost basis has materially  changed,  staff  proposes  a specific  revision.
Where  costs remain  broadly  aligned  but inflation  has reduced  recovery,  a uniform  7% adjustment
is proposed  as an interim  measure  pending  any future,  detailed  cost-of-service  studies.

The attached  Master  Fee and Charges  Schedule  is organized  by department  and service  area and
shows  the  current  and  proposed  fee.  Annotations  identify  fees  excluded  from  the  baseline
adjustment  and those subject  to external  limits.  Technical  edits (e.g., clari'Jying  units  of  measure,

adding  account  references,  aligning  titles  to current  practice)  are included.

Unless  adopted  as an urgent  measure  necessary  to protect  public  health,  safety,  or welfare,  fee
changes  take effect  60 days after Council  adoption.  If adopted  on September  9, 2025, the effective
date will  be November  9, 2025.

NOTICE  REQUIREMENT:  Notice  of this Public  Hearing  was published  in the Los  Angeles
WAVE  on August  14, 2025, and August  21, 2025, and circulated  via the City web page, Facebook,
Instagram,  and Twitter.

TIMING  REQUIREMENT:  When  local  agencies  want to increase  their fees or charges,  Section
66018  of the California  Government  Code requires  a public  hearing  to be conducted,  at which  time
oral or written  presentations  can be made,  as part of a regularly  scheduled  meeting.  At least 10
days prior  to the meeting,  the local  agency  shall make  available  to the public  data indicating  the
amount  of cost, or estimated  cost,  required  to provide  the service  for which  the fee or service
charge  is levied  and the revenue  sources  anticipated  to provide  the service.  The notice  shall be for
ten (10) days, and the notices  shall  be published  at least twice  with  five  (5) days separating  the
notices,  not counting  the dates of publications.  The change  in fees shall be effective  sixty  (60) days
after the final  adoption  of the Council,  unless  passed as an urgent  measure  to protect  the public's
health,  welfare,  and safety.  The schedule  is as follows:

First  Day  of Public  Notice  in Local  Publication  August  14, 2025
Date  Fee Data  is Provided  to Public  August  15, 2025
Second  Day  of Public  Notice  in Local  Publication  August  21, 2025
Public  Hearing  September  9, 2025
Date  of Implementation  of New Fees  November  9, 2025

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  AMENDED  AND  RESTATED  JOINT
POWERS  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE  LOS  ANGELES  GATEWAY  REGION
INTEGRATED  REGIONAL  WATER  MANAGEMENT  JOINT  POWER  AUTHORITY
AND  APPROVAL  OF THE  JOINT  POWERS  AGREEMENT

PURPOSE:  The  City  Council  is requested  to approve  an updated  Joint  Powers  Agreement
with  the  Los  Angeles  Gateway  Region  Water  Management  Authority.  The  new  agreement
updates  governance  rules  and  membership  while  keeping  South  Gate  an active  partner  in
regional  water  projects  until  the City  elects  to withdraw.  Approval  ensures  the City  continues  to
benefit  from  collaboration  and grant funding  opportunities.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  approving  the Amended  and Restated  Joint  Powers  Agreement
  with  the Los  Angeles  Gateway  Region  Integrated  Regional  Water  Management  Joint
  Powers  Authority,  thereby  reaffirming  the  City's  participation  and  continuing
  membership  until  such time  the City  elects  to withdraw,  which  has aru'iual  membership
  dues of $15,000;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The annual  dues are $15,000  and
budgeted  with  Measure  W as a part of the annual  operating  department  budget.

ANALYSIS:  The  City  of  South  Gate  is  a member  of  the  Los  Angeles  Gateway  Region
Integrated  Regional  Water  Management  Joint  Powers  Authority  ("GWMA"),  which  was
established  in 2007  through  a Joint  Powers  Authority  Agreement  ("JPA").  The  GWMA  was
formed  in response  to the State's  initiative,  which  gives priority  for competitive  grant funding  to
projects  that are regional  in scope, involve  multiple  agencies,  and provide  multiple  benefits.

Since its inception,  GWMA's  membership,  scope, and responsibilities  have expanded,  prompting
an amendment  to the JPA Agreement  to better  reflect  current  and anticipated  activities.  On April
10, 2025, the Governing  Board  approved  the attached  Amended  and Restated  JPA Agreement  by

 a super-majority  vote,  and  each  member  agency  is now  requested  to  formally  adopt  it  as
presented.

BACKGROUND:  GWMA  was formed  in 2007  to improve  water  supply  reliability,  protect
water  quality,  and address  stormwater  and flood  control  needs  in the Gateway  Region  of Los
Angeles  County.  Serving  a population  of more than two million  people,  GWMA's  member  cities
and water  agencies  work  together  to plan  and implement  regional  projects  and to secure  local,
state, and federal  :tunding.

Membership  includes  28  cities  and  water  agencies  from  across  the  Gateway  region,  each
representing  unique  geographic,  demographic,  political,  and economic  conditions.  By  speaking
with  one  voice,  GWMA  effectively  communicates  the  region's  needs,  strengthening
opportunities  for partnerships  and funding.

In addition  to developing  regional  projects  and pursuing  grants,  GWMA  plays  an active  role in
the  Greater  Los  Angeles  County  Integrated  Regional  Water  Management  Program  (GLA
IRWMP),  ensuring  the  Gateway  region's  priorities  are represented.  The  GLA  IRWMP  is a
collaborative  planning  effort  among  public  agencies,  non-profits,  and  other  stakeholders  to
identi:[y,  prioritize,  and implement  water  resource  projects  that  provide  regional  benefits  and
meet state water  management  objectives.

Since  2012,  GWMA  has also  coordinated  and provided  administrative  support  for  watershed
groups  working  to meet  stormwater  quality  requirements  under  the State's  MS4  Permit  for the
Lower  Los Angeles  River,  Lower  San Gabriel  River,  Los  Cerritos  Channel,  and other  regional
areas.

The City  of South  Gate has been a member  since  August  15, 2007,  when  the JPA  Agreement
(Contract  No. 2394)  was approved  by the City  Council.

In 2024,  GWMA  staff  and legal  counsel  proposed  updates  to the JPA  Agreement,  including:
establishing  board member  terms  and allowing  up to three alternates;  updating  the list of member
cities/agencies;  defining  a super-majority  vote for certain  actions;  and removing  the requirement
for  a lead  agency  to  conduct  GWMA's  financial  and  contractual  affairs,  which  have  been
handled  in-house  since 2014.

On April  10, 2025,  GWMA  staff  presented  the revised  draft  agreement  to the GWMA  Board,
incorporating  member  comments.  The  Board  approved  the  Amended  and  Restated  JPA
Agreement  by super-majority  vote, and it is now presented  for City  Council  consideration.

  SUBJECT:  RENEWAL  OF AGREEMENT  WITH  AXON  ENTERPRISE,  INC.  FOR  BODY-
  WORN  CAMERAS  FOR  THE  POLICE  DEPARTMENT.

  PURPOSE:  To approve  the renewal  of a 5-year  agreement  with  Axon  Enterprise,  Inc. for the Police
  Department's  Body-Worn  Camera  Program.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a. Approving  the renewal  of the Agreement  with  Axon  Enterprise,  Inc. for the continued  use of
  body-worn  cameras  and related  accessories  for police  department  personnel;  and
  b. Approving  the issuance  of a purchase  order  to Axon  Enterprise,  Inc.  for  ongoing  program
  implementation  and support.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The total  cost for  the 5-year
  agreement  is $688,324.  Funding  for the current  year in the amount  of $149,923  is included  in the FY
  25/26  budget  in the Asset  Forfeiture.  Future  program  costs will  continue  to be covered  through  Asset
  Forfeiture  and/or  additional  grant opportunities  as they become  available.

  ANALYSIS:  The  City  Council  previously  approved  the implementation  of a body-worn  camera
  program  for  police  department  personnel,  selecting  Axon  Enterprise,  Inc.  as the service  provider
  following  a comprehensive  evaluation  process.  The program  has since become  an integral  part of the
  Police  Department's  operations,  improving  transparency,  accountability,  and officer  safety.

  Axon  continues  to be the industry  leader  in body-worn  camera  technology  and data management.  The
  company  provides  the most  comprehensive  service  package,  including  equipment,  cloud-based  data
  storage,  software,  training,  and technical  support.  Renewing  the agreement  ensures  uninterrupted
  service,  protects  continuity  of digital  evidence  management,  and maintains  compliance  with  current
  standards  of best practice.

  Since the program's  inception,  body-worn  cameras  have demonstrated  significant  value  to the Police
  Department  and the community  by:

  *  Increasing  public  trust and transparency.
  *  Reducing  unfounded  complaints  and liability  claims.
  Improving  officer  and cornrnunity  safety.

  *  Enhancing  training  opportunities  through  real-world  video  review.

in 2021  as part  of a phased  approach  to expand  transparency  and accountability  in policing.  The
program  has been well  received  by both officers  and the community  and has proven  to be an effective
tool in enhancing  the Department's  legitimacy.

 SUBJECT:  APPROVE  A PROFESSIONAL  SERVICE  AGREEMENT  WITH  WILLDAN
 ENGINEERING  FOR  A TEMPORARY  CODE  ENFORCEMENT  SUPERVISOR  AND
 REAJ'PROPRIATION  OF FUNDS

 PURPOSE:  To request  City  Council  approval  of a professional  service  agreement  (Agreement)  with
 Willdan  Engineering  to provide  one temporary  Code  Enforcement  Supervisor  for  an initial  four-
 month  period,  with  an option  for  a one-month  extension  and to approve  the reappropriation  of
 $88,000 from Salaries (Account  No. 100-604-29-5101)  to Professional  Services  (Account  No. 100-
 604-29-6101)  to fund the Agreement.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  It is recommended  that the City  Council:
  a. Approve  an Agreement  with  Willdan  Engineering  to provide  one Code Enforcement
  Supervisor  for an initial  term of four-months,  with  the option  to extend  the Agreement  for
  one additional  month,  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney;
  b. Authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  and any necessary  amendments  or
  extensions;  and
  c. Approve  the reappropriation  of $88,000  from  Salaries  (Account  No. 100-604-29-5101)  to
  Professional  Services  (Account  No. 100-604-29-6101)  to fund  the contract.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no negative  fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The Agreement  will  be
 'funded  entirely  via  salary  savings  from  the  vacant  Code  Enforcement  Supervisor  and  Code
 Enforcement  Officer  positions.

 To facilitate  this,  staff recommends  reappropriating  $88,000  from  Salaries  (Account  No. 100-604-
 29-5101)  to Professional  Services  (Account  No.  100-604-29-6101).  This  action  will  ensure  the
 availability  of funds  to pay Willdan  Engineering  for temporary  staffing,  which  will  be charged  at a
 Code Enforcement  Supervisor  rate at $110 an hour.

 ANALYSIS:  Willdan  Engineering  is a vetted  municipal  services  contractor  with  experience
 supplying  qualified  Code Enforcement  Supervisors

  221
 The contractor-supplied  Code Enforcement  Supervisor  will:

  *  Oversee  daily  operations  and supervise  Code Enforcement  Officers
  *  Investigate  potential  violations,  document  cases, and initiate  enforcement  actions
  *  Ensure  compliance  with  municipal  codes (zoning,  property  maintenance,  signage,
  abandoned  vehicles,  etc.)
  *  Coordinate  with  other City  departments  and serve as a technical  resource

  *  Maintain  continuity  of service  while  permanent  recruitment  is in progress

The agreementterm  is four-months,  with  an option  for a one-month  extension  ifthe  permanent  hiring
process  requires  additional  time.  Should  the  permanent  selection  process  conclude  early,  the
extension  option  need not be utilized.

BACKGROUND:  The Code Enforcement  Division  is current  operating  with  four unfiled  positions:
two Code Enforcement  Officers,  one Senior  Code Enforcement  Officer,  and the Code Enforcement
Supervisor.  Two  key vacancies  are the result  of recent  retirements  - specifically  one Senior  Code
Enforcement  Officer  and  one  Code  Enforcement  Officer  -  leaving  the  Division  critically
understaffed.

The Code Enforcement  Supervisor  position  is a critical  leadership  role responsible  for overseeing
code investigations,  case management,  enforcement  coordination,  and ensuring  compliance  with
applicable  laws  and  regulations.  At  present,  this  position  remains  vacant,  and  recruitment  is
underway.  The permanent  Code Enforcement  Supervisor  position  was posted  on July 31, 2025, with
applications  accepted  through  August  28, 2025.

Given  the  anticipated  timeline  for  candidate  screening,  interviews,  and  onboarding,  interim
supervisory  support  is necessary  to maintain  service  levels  and operational  oversight  during  this
transitional  period.  To  address  this  need,  staff  is proposing  to utilize  the  services  of  Willdan
Engineering,  a qualified  municipal  services  provider  with  the capacity  to provide  an experienced
Code Enforcement  Supervisor  on a temporary  basis.

 Introduction

The City of South Gate is requesting  qualified  firms to submit  a proposal  for on-call consulting  services  for
future  development  projects  and economic  development  efforts  including,  but not limited  to, general
plan amendments,  code  amendments,  rezoning,  tentative  subdivision  maps,  conditional  use permits,
design reviews,  plan reviews,  specific  plans, environmental  services,  and economic  development.  The City
anticipates  selecting  firms  to provide  consulting  services  on an on-call  basis, and that  each firm  may
subsequently  be asked to prepare  specific  proposals  for more than one project.  Services needed  include:

  *  Planning,  zoning,  and land use services
  *  Landscape  plan review  for compliance  with the water  efficient  landscape  ordinance
  *  Environmental  services  in compliance  with the California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA)
  *  Economic  development  advisory  services

Interested  consultants  are not  required  to  provide  all services  but  only  those  that  the  consultant
specializes  in and can provide.  The City anticipates  compiling  a list of several  consultants  in various
disciplines  to be available  on an on-call  basis.

Planning  Consultants
The City occasionally  requires  updates  to its General  Plan, zoning  code, specific  plans, and other  planning
documents.  The City seeks consultants  who can provide  these  planning  services  on an as-needed  basis.
Consultants  may be asked to present  workshops  and training  sessions  with  the  Planning  Commission
and/or City Council.

Environmental  Consultants
The State of California  has an environmental  statute  called California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA).
The National  Environmental  Policy Act (NEPA) is a United  States  Environmental  law that  promotes  the
enhancement  of the  environment  and established  the  President's  Council  on Environmental  Quality
(CEQ). Both laws require  state and local agencies  to identify  the significant  environmental  impacts  of their
actions  and avoid or mitigate  those  impacts,  if feasible.

The consultant(s)  selected  will be responsible  for the preparation  of Environmental  Impact  Reports  (EIR),
Environmental  Impact  Statements  (ELS), Negative  Declarations,  Mitigated  Negative  Declarations,  technical
studies  and other  California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA) and National  Environmental  Policy Act
(NEPA) documentation  for proposed  projects. The consultant/s will be willing to work collaboratively  with,
and manage  the work  of, other  members  of the environmental  analysis team.

Landscape  Consultants
New development  and retrofitted  landscape  water  efficiency  standards  are governed  by the Model  Water
Efficient  Landscape  Ordinance  (MWELO).  The MWELO  is also referenced  by Title 24, Part 11, Chapters  4
and 5 CalGreen  Building  Code. All local agencies  must  adopt,  implement,  and enforce  the MWELO  or a
local Water  Efficient  Landscape  Ordinance  (WELO) that is at least as effective  as the MWELO.  Usually,  local
agencies  that adopt  WELOs create  a more stringent  ordinance  than MWELO.

The City of South  Gate  has a Water  Conservation  Ordinance  adopted  in 2009  that  promotes  water
conservation  measures  but may not fully meet the requirements  of MWELO.  Thus, the City must rely and
implement  the State's  MWELO.

  3

  239
 The  City  is seeking  guidance  from  landscape  consultants  on  adopting  a local  WELO  or  continuing
implementing  the standards  in the State  MWELO.  Furthermore,  the City is seeking  consultants  to review
plans  for  MWELO  compliance,  which  includes  but  is not  limited  to reviewing  landscape  and  irrigation
plans,  providing  recommendations  on  improving  water  efficiency  measures,  conducting  compliance
inspections,  and finalizing  permits.

Economic  Development  Consultants
The City is seeking  a consultant  to provide  advisory  services  on economic  development.  Occasionally,  the
City requires  economic  development  data for decision-makers  and requires  a consultant  that  specializes
in economics  and market  conditions.  The City seeks  consultants  who  can provide  these  services  on an as-
needed  basis.  Consultants  may  be asked  to present  workshops  and training  sessions  with  the  Planning
Commission and/or City Council.

Project  Overview

The purpose  of this  RFQ is to solicit  and select  a firm(s)  to provide  consultant  services  to assist City staff
as it relates  to various  planning,  landscaping,  environmental,  and economic  development  issues.  Under
the direction  of the City's  Community  Development  Director,  the consultant(s)  will  provide  the  range  of
expertise  to carry out the  normal  functions  of the  necessary review  process and/or  program
implementation.  All services  provided  by the consultant(s)  shall  be performed  by individuals  who  meet
the qualifications,  education, and certification/Iicensing  for the position(s). The successful consultant(s)
shall  also  have  the  resources  to  provide  cost  effective  and  timely  services,  including  providing
outstanding  customer  service  to the City and its related  clients.

  SUBJECT:  PURCHASE  ORDER  WITH  INTERGRAPmCS  COMPANY  PRINTER  TO
  PRODUCE  THE  CITY'S  CONNECT  BROCHURE  FOR  FY 2025/26.

  PURPOSE:  The purpose  of this item  is to obtain  City  Council  approval  to issue a Purchase  Order
  to Intergraphics  Company  Printer  for  the production,  printing,  folding,  and mailing  of the City's
  Connect  brochure  for Fiscal  Year  2025/26.  This  brochure  is a vital  communication  tool  that helps
  keep residents  informed  about  City  programs,  services,  events,  and community  updates.  Approval  is
  required  as the total  contract  amount  exceeds  the City's  $50,000  procurement  threshold.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:
  a. Approve  a Purchase  Order  with  Intergraphics  Company  Printer  in the amount  of $71,000
  (for four 40-page  quarterly  brochures  at $17,750  each) to print,  fold,  and mail  the City's
  Connect  brochure;  and
  b. Authorize  the City's  Purchasing  Division  to issue a Purchase  Order  for this process  in
  accordance  with  the City's  purchasing  ordinance  and policies;  and
  c. Authorize  the Director  of Parks  & Recreation  to execute  any additional  documents  as may be
  required  for 'future  issues of the Connect.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Funds  for  the "Connect"  are already  included  in  the  current  budget;  no
  additional  appropriation  is required

  REPORT  SUMMARY:  The  Parks  &  Recreation  Department,  in  collaboration  with  the  City
  Manager's  Office,  produces  four  (4)  quarterly  issues  of the "Connect"  City  News  and Parks  &
  Recreation  Guide  each year.  This  40-page  brochure  serves  as a key  communication  tool  to keep
  South  Gate  residents  informed  about  upcoming  programs  and events,  including  aquatics,  fitness,
  sports,  Cultural  Arts,  youth  and teen programs,  senior  activities,  and seasonal  celebrations  such as
  Halloween,  Easter  Fest, Winter  Wonderland  and the 4th of July  Carnival  and fireworks  display.  It
  also  provides  important  community  updates,  such  as passport  services,  holiday  trash  collection
  schedules,  street sweeping  notifications,  and City  construction  projects.

  Each  issue  is mailed  directly  to over  25,000  households,  with  additional  copies  made  available  at
  local parks,  City  Hall,  and public  libraries.

total of six (6) quotes were received.  Upon  evaluation,  the bid was awarded  to Intergraphics
Company  for their  40-page  option  as the most responsive  and responsible  bidder.

As the total purchase  amount  of $71,000  (4 issues x $17,750)  exceeds  the City's  $50,000
procurement  threshold,  City  Council  approval  is required  to proceed  with  the issuance  of the
purchase  order.

minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

CALL TO ORDER  Maria Davila, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:30 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Maria Davila, Vice Mayor Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria
  del Pilar Avalos, Council Member Gil Hurtado and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

1
FINANCIAL MGMT  The City Council:

  a. Adopted Resolution No. 2025-26-CC entitled Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of South Gate, California, establishing a new
  Schedule of Fees for City services effective for FY 2025-26;

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Resolution in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney; and

  c. Rescinding Resolution No. 2021-51-CC

  Rob Houston, City Manager, stated there is a presentation on the fee
  schedule, and Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services will
  present the presentation.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services, presented the proposed
  master fee schedule for Fiscal Year 2025-26 and requested City Council’s
  approval of the resolution establishing the updated fees for city services
  and rescinding the city’s prior fee resolution from 2021.

  Mayor Davila asked if anyone in the audience wished to speak on this
  item.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue, is not in support of raising city fees. As to the
  electronic public records request fees, it wasn’t uncommon to pay for
  copies.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

1
FINANCIAL MGMT
CONT’D  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Davila closed the audience
  portion.

EMAILS  Mario Dominguez requested City Council to eliminate fees for emailed
  public records request, adopt a Quimby fee for ordinance to fund parks
  and recreation, remove the $3 bicycle license fee and stop the increase in
  the body warn camera footage fee.

  Council Member Hurtado requested not raising the preferential parking
  fee. He addressed the code enforcement fees and did not see fees
  regarding electric vehicles on sidewalks.

  Chief Arakawa stated the police department are working on an education
  campaign.

  Council Member Avalos stated that the preferential parking fee is only 7%.
  It is not a huge difference, but Code Enforcement is something to look at.

  Council Member Avalos motioned to approve the master fee schedule with
  the exception of Code Enforcement and seconded by Council Member
  Hurtado.

  Mr. Frausto asked for clarification on the motion.

  Mr. Houston stated it was mentioned perhaps freezing one of the fees and
  then a counterproposal of not freezing the preferential parking. Then how
  to handle from a policy perspective a repeat offender but the actual fee
  that’s being proposed to have a slight increase for the code enforcement
  fine.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA Juan Rosas Castaneda, 2450 Illinois Avenue, complained about the new
  water meter.

  Claudia Rivera is dissatisfied with Councilwoman Avalos’ character.

  Ana, Director of the South Gate Chamber of Commerce, thanked everyone
  for joining the job fair. 452 people attended the job fair. She mentioned
  Northgate has been providing vouchers for food insecurity to the
  community. She mentioned the State of the City address hosted Thursday,
  November 6th at the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium and the Children’s
  Christmas Lane Parade is Sunday, December 14th.

  Page 2 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
CONT’D  Sonia, South Gate resident, stated there was an accident at the corner of
  State Street and Illinois Avenue and a community member passed away
  due to lack of a pedestrian walk.

  Armando Velasquez, Independence Avenue, announced upcoming events
  with the Kiwanis Club of South Gate. He also mentioned having issues
  with emails from Kiwanis to City Hall.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue, is the Vice Chair for the Parks Commission,
  and reiterated the importance of working with partner organizations and
  emphasized the people are volunteers. She is disappointed with the
  comments made by Councilwoman Avalos relating to auditing the
  buildings.

  Candace Solache, Tweedy Boulevard, echoed the sentiments that Ms. Ruiz
  expressed.

  Alan Flores, Chairman of the Parks Commission mentioned all the
  organizations and volunteers are important. He is also disappointed with
  all the social media attacking City Council.

  Maria Hernandez thanked everyone that replied to her email regarding
  Circle Park and the residents’ concerns.

EMAILS  Mario Dominguez requesting that the city install bike racks on its public
  transportation vans.

  South Gate Junior Athletic Association, South Gate Aztecs Youth Football,
  South Gate AYSO Region 652, South Gate Aqua Coalition, and South
  Gate Boy and Cub Scout submitted a joint letter urging the City Council to
  protect affordable access to city facilities that support youth programs.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works Department, addressed the
  comments from the audience regarding the charging station by the Civic
  Center, water meters and Circle Park. He also mentioned the residential
  resurfacing project is making lots of progress.

  Council Member Hurtado asked that the cross issue be addressed.

  Mr. Cervantes mentioned the intersection has certain traffic controls and
  the city is planning to re-stripe.

  City Attorney Salinas stated the cause of the incident was not anything
  having to do with the striping of the streets or conditions of the streets.

  Page 3 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation, invited everyone to the
  new Teen Center location in the Girls Clubhouse on September 15th from
  3-6 p.m. He mentioned an issue with the pool due to a power outage in the
  city and then cascaded down to other issues. It will be closed through the
  end of September. He also mentioned having a fireworks show during
  Halloween on October 31st.

  Gabriel Perez, Director of Community Development, had no updates.

  Luis Frausto, Director of Administrative Services, had no updates.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Services, had no updates.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police reported that this past Thursday, three
  police officer recruits graduated, which will start field training. There will
  be a car show in two weeks at South Gate Park. The Trunk and Treat is
  scheduled for Thursday, October 30th in front of city hall. The Pageant of
  the Trees meeting is coming up shortly.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, stated the city has amazing facilities that the
  community gets great use of, but very expensive to operate as they get
  older.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, nothing to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, nothing to report.

  Council Member Avalos thanked everyone present tonight and also on
  YouTube. She had the pleasure of attending the Rotary. She thanked
  Northgate for matching their donations with the community’s donations.
  She will be attending the Vector Control meeting this week.

  Council Member Avalos stated that no one from the JAA has made a
  meaningful response to any of her questions she believes lies at the heart
  of the personal attacks she has been receiving. She formally requested a
  valuation, and she is requesting it again on record. She has not received a
  response to the requested valuation and documentation.

  Council Member Avalos spoke on leadership and second chances. She
  does not believe in blacklisting people for saying critical things about her
  in the past or disagree and act like a dictator. The recent appointment
  being discussed or brought up, is not based on personal history or to stop
  someone from criticizing her. The individual in question has previously
  served on the commission and has demonstrated both experience and

  Page 4 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  dedication to the community. This individual has provided information to
  the community during the ICE raids. She is asking to move forward with
  integrity, compassion, and renewed focus on what really matters most,
  which is the well-being of this community.

  Council Member Hurtado stated the Rotary Club had a nice event. ICE
  raids might get worse due to the Supreme Court’s decision. He explained
  that any city projects close to where he resides, by law he must recuse
  himself.

  Council Member Rios hopes there can be some compromise with SCE
  regarding Circle Park and the residents. He attended the school safety
  collaborative with the Mayor and it was well attended. He is saddened the
  swimming pool is closed for a month. The job fair was well attended. He
  thanked Northgate for providing food vouchers.

  Vice Mayor Barron is the President of the SELA Kiwanis and mentioned
  upcoming events (September 30th will be the Second Annual College Fair
  and Career Fair at the Henry C. Gonzalez Auditorium from 5:00 p.m. to
  8:00 p.m. There will be over 27 universities, colleges, and workforce
  development organizations. September 20th is going to be the SELA day of
  service.)

  Vice Mayor Barron visited the residents on Karmont regarding Circle
  Park. He urges families to have a preparation plan in place due to the
  Supreme Court’s decision to remove the temporary restraining order.

  Mayor Davila attended the Chamber of Commerce and Veterans Resource
  fair and was very impressed by how well it was attended. She also
  attended the Gateway Cities COG retreat and the three main topics
  discussed were transportation, broadband and homelessness. She thanked
  the public for attending tonight’s meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 were unanimously approved by motion
  of Council Member Avalos and seconded by Council Member Hurtado.
  Item 8 was pulled for separate discussion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Barron, yes; Mayor Davila,
  yes.

  Page 5 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
2
WATER  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Resolution No. 2025-27-CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of South Gate, California, approving the Amended and
  Restated Joint Powers Agreement (Contract No. 2394) with the Los
  Angeles Gateway Region Integrated Regional Water Management
  Joint Powers Authority, thereby reaffirming the City’s participation
  and continuing membership until such time the City elects to
  withdraw, which has annual membership dues of $15,000; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

3
COMMUNITY DEV/
HOUSING  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Amendment No. 5 to Contract No. 2020-19-CC with RSG, Inc., to
  continue providing as-needed services to the Community Development
  Department effective July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, with
  potential two one-year extensions in an amount not to exceed
  $125,000; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 5 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.
4
LAW ENFORCEMENT  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. The renewal of the Agreement (Contract No. 2021-122-CC) with Axon
  Enterprise, Inc. for the continued use of body-worn cameras and
  related accessories for police department personnel; and

  b. The issuance of a purchase order to Axon Enterprise, Inc. for ongoing
  program implementation and support.
5
CODE ENFORCEMENT
ADMIN  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B & C during Consent
  Calendar:

  a. Agreement (Contract No. 2025-58-CC) with Willdan Engineering to
  provide one Code Enforcement Supervisor for an initial term of four-
  months, with the option to extend the Agreement for one additional
  month, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney;

  Page 6 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

5
CODE ENFORCEMENT
ADMIN CONT’D
  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement and any necessary
  amendments or extensions; and

  c. The reappropriation of $88,000 from Salaries (Account No. 100-604-
  29-5101) to Professional Services (Account No. 100-604-29-6101) to
  fund the contract.

6
LAND USE PLANNING
